newsitem.title: USA: Heartstream to do most of own marketing.
newsitem.headline: Heartstream to do most of own marketing.

text.p: Heartstream Inc is seeking partners to help sell light-weight external defibrillator to smaller markets but is keeping the lion's share of the marketing to itself, a senior executive said on Thursday.
The Seattle-based company on Thursday said it got U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for its ForeRunner automatic external defibrillator to treat victims of sudden cardiac arrest.

The company is building a 12-member sales force for the fire, ambulance, police, industry and transport markets, which represent about 80 percent of the device's sales potential, Keith Serzen, Heartstream's vice president of sales and marketing, said in an interview.

He said the company was targeting major medical device companies to sign distribution agreements for the hospital and physician office markets. But the large companies "want more market than we're willing to give them," he said.

Nevertheless, he said the company anticipated signing partnership deals by the fourth quarter or 1997's first quarter. ForeRunner is expected to cost between $3,000 and $4,000 to put into service, Heartstream said. Most current automatic external defibrillators cost between $5,000 and $7,500, the company said.
Serzen listed the company's chief competitors as Physio-Control Holding Corp, SurVivaLink Corp SVLK.O and Laerdal Medical Corp.
He attributed the company's stock on Thursday jump to expectations among some investors that the Heartstream device would face a longer FDA approval process.
The company on Thursday booked its first ForeRunner order with the fire department in Issaquah, Wash, Serzen said.
